I graded `submissions/s2.json` for quiz 0001 and wrote `grades/0001-s2.json`. I wrote the file as a copy of the draft but didn't read it back to check the JSON. I did read the draft back, and it had an entry for every item.

| Item | Verdict | Misconception |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | none |
| q2 | correct | none |
| q3 | wrong | M6 |
| q4 | partial | M4 |
| q5 | correct | none |
| q6 | partial | none |

- **q3:** Riley chose "it will eventually fix the bug". If the same edit keeps failing with the same error, more steps add nothing. The fix is a step limit.
- **q4:** The answer 4 is right, but Riley's reason says the model runs the tools itself. The model only requests them, and the program runs them.
- **q6:** "By the name" is only part of it. The model also reads each tool's description and parameters.

**Summary:** You have the agent loop down, and you know the model requests tools rather than running them. Two things to fix: an agent needs a stopping condition, and the model picks tools from their descriptions, not just their names. Next, redo q6 by writing which parts of the check_calendar tool description (name, what it does, parameters) the model reads to choose it.

The review loop ran two passes, and I applied the fixes from both to the draft. I did not run a third review. I left "Not quite." as the opener on q3, because the grade skill requires it, and I left q4's feedback over three sentences because it walks through the full run. Both are in `review-records/0001-s2-grade.md`.

I added `learning-records/0003-agent-loop-recalled-after-four-days.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s1.json` is still not graded.
